theMeasurement.byWhichRun: MEASURED ABSENCE, stated as one: NO retired parcel-node atom in any of the six counties carries a run id. `body ? 'retiredRunId'` -> 0 of 1013 (Bastrop) and 0 of 40 (Travis); same for 'retiredByRun'. The provenance a retired row actually carries is `retiredAt` (one single timestamp per county, i.e. one run) plus `retiredReason` plus `sourceVintage`. The retirement run therefore CANNOT be named from the atom store, and this lane does not guess one. For the serve-side population the run id IS carried (`publishRunId`) and is reported.

theTwoQuestionsThisLaneHasToAnswerBefore.Q1: Does a usable public cadastral service exist for the county?
theTwoQuestionsThisLaneHasToAnswerBefore.Q2: Is the field it exposes in the SAME identifier namespace as the node id?
theTwoQuestionsThisLaneHasToAnswerBefore.whyQ2IsTheRealOne: A source that answers in the ACCOUNT namespace corroborates nothing: it would 'confirm live' every account-keyed row and 'deny' every map-keyed row, i.e. it would invert the answer. The 2026-09-13 ruling (Hays node id is the parcel-map id) plus _catalog/tx_cad_source_registry.json (Hays row: format 'honest_absent', auth_posture 'absent', verified 2026-08-09) is exactly the trap, and the registry is stale in the other direction too.
theTwoQuestionsThisLaneHasToAnswerBefore.theTestThatDecidesIt: Take REAL node ids out of the atoms store for the county (active AND retired), ask the county's own service for each by the candidate field, and require a NEGATIVE CONTROL to answer 0. A field that answers 1 for every sampled real node id and 0 for a fabricated control id is the node-id namespace. Anything else is not registered.
theTwoQuestionsThisLaneHasToAnswerBefore.howIKnowTheNodeIdIsTxgioPropId: The node id is `{county_fips}:{parcelKey}` (plan-county-parcel-nodes.ts, `plan.planned.map(p => `${plan.countyFips}:${p.parcelKey}`)`) and parcelKey comes from txgio_parcel.prop_id, geo_id or a synthetic feature key. Measured on the store: the id shapes differ by county and each shape matches the corresponding txgio column -- Bastrop numbers ('48021:21936'), Caldwell numbers ('48055:10008'), Hays integers ('48209:100002'), McLennan integers ('48309:100000'), Williamson R-stems ('48491:R000009'), Travis MIXED (integers AND '48453:_feature-stratmap25-landparcels-48453-travis-202508-626886').

D1_tri_stateReadingInsteadOfBoolean.change: `decideRetiredParcelNodeReactivations(review, liveCurrency)` gains a third reading. A candidate's reading is one of 'live' | 'absent' | 'unmeasured'; `boolean` is still accepted (true -> live, false -> absent) so no existing caller changes, and an id MISSING from the map is now 'unmeasured' rather than 'absent'.
D1_tri_stateReadingInsteadOfBoolean.verdictShape: `{ reactivate, confirmedAbsent, unmeasured, stillRetired }` where `stillRetired` is the union of confirmedAbsent and unmeasured, kept so every existing consumer keeps working.
D1_tri_stateReadingInsteadOfBoolean.whyThisIsForcedAndNotDecorative: DEV_PROCESS and the contract both say an empty result is NOT an absence and that every absence carries its basis. The shipped code collides an id the source answered 'no' about with an id nobody asked about, and the CLI then prints `liveCurrencySource: 'none-registered'` beside a stillRetired list that reads like a measurement. The dispatch's falsifier 2 ('a county whose live source is unreachable reports UNMEASURED, never zero candidates') is exactly this defect.
D1_tri_stateReadingInsteadOfBoolean.theExistingTestThatMustChangeAndWhyThatI: re-acquisition-contract.test.ts 'FALSIFIER: an empty live-currency map (no corroboration attempted) reactivates nothing' currently asserts `stillRetired` == [{parcelNodeId, reason: contains 'NOT confirmed live'}]. Under D1 an empty map means UNMEASURED, and 'NOT confirmed live' is precisely the false inference being fixed. The assertion moves to `unmeasured` with a reason naming that no reading was taken. The load-bearing half -- zero reactivations -- is unchanged, and is asserted in both the old and the new test.

D2_sourcesAreInjectedNotImported.change: the registry moves behind a small shared helper, `county-parcel-id-currency.mjs`, exporting `makeArcgisIdCurrencySource({ url, idField })`: chunked `where <idField> IN (...)` queries (chunk 100), `returnGeometry=false`, `f=json`, paged with resultOffset when a chunk matches more than maxRecordCount rows, one retry on a transport error, and a request counter the run summary reports.
D2_sourcesAreInjectedNotImported.why: The dispatch says 'page politely, cache, and state your request count'. A full-layer download per county (which is what the Bastrop path does, ~33 requests for 65k features) is affordable ONLY because Bastrop's layer is small; Travis (386,682) and Williamson (290,344) are not. A chunked IN query costs 1 request per 100 candidates, so a whole review is ~11 requests for Bastrop's 1,013 and ~1 per county elsewhere, and the count is measurable.
D2_sourcesAreInjectedNotImported.idNormalization: ids are normalized with the SAME `normalizeParcelKeyToken` the planner uses (leading zeros stripped from all-digit keys), so a zero-padded source row and a zero-padded node id still address the same parcel. The Bastrop path already does this via `normalizePropId`.
D2_sourcesAreInjectedNotImported.failureMode: a source that throws (DNS, timeout, HTTP 5xx, non-JSON body) propagates to the CLI, which marks EVERY candidate of that county UNMEASURED with the transport reason. It does NOT become an empty map, and it does NOT become zero candidates.

D3_reportOnlyIsTheDefaultAndApplyIsGuard.change: no new flag for report-only: the existing default (no --apply) IS report-only and already prints the full summary. The summary gains `confirmedLive`, `confirmedAbsent`, `unmeasured`, `unmeasuredReasons`, `liveCurrencySource` ('registered' | 'none-registered' | 'unreachable'), `liveCurrencyRequests`, `retiredShareBefore`, and `retiredShareAfterHypotheticalReactivation` (with its denominator named).
D3_reportOnlyIsTheDefaultAndApplyIsGuard.why: dispatch item 3 names exactly these five figures; four of them did not exist.

D4_blastRadiusRefusalOnReactivation.change: the apply path calls P-213's `evaluateBlastRadius` BEFORE taking the write lease, with `writer='parcel-node-retired-review-reactivation'`, `scopeKey=county`, `affected=verdict.reactivate.length`, `population=review.priorRetired`, and a declared `MAX_REACTIVATION_SHARE`. The CLI also accepts `--blast-radius-override=<token>`, passed through to the guard's `override` argument, falling back to `process.env.BLAST_RADIUS_OVERRIDE`.
D4_blastRadiusRefusalOnReactivation.whyThisSpecificControlRatherThanANewOne: writer-blast-radius-guard.mjs's own header, bypass list item (c), names THIS call site as an unguarded bypass: '"review-retired-parcel-nodes.mjs's reactivation path -- the opposite direction (retired -> active) and out of THIS module's scope". ENFORCEMENT says a mass state change refuses before it lands. Wiring the existing, already-proven control closes a bypass the control itself documents, instead of inventing a second threshold convention beside it.
D4_blastRadiusRefusalOnReactivation.declaredNumber: MAX_REACTIVATION_SHARE = 0.05, the same declared number write-parcel-node-county.mjs uses for MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE, and for the same reason: P-212 reactivated 56,691 of 57,704 retired rows (98.25%) in one run with no share check anywhere. The DENOMINATOR is the retired population the reactivation is drawn from -- the same 'the population a caller measures is exactly the denominator its own share claim depends on' rule the guard's header states.
D4_blastRadiusRefusalOnReactivation.consequenceStatedOutLoud: under 0.05, ANY reactivation of more than 5 percent of a county's retired rows refuses and requires the exact measured token. That is the intended behaviour, and it means the integration seat's authorised reactivation is a two-step act: run report-only to read the counts, then re-execute with the token those counts print. The reactivation command is emitted in the close with its count for exactly this reason.

D5_noReactivateNoWriteNoDeploy.change: none -- the dispatch forbids it and this lane does not do it. --apply is never passed in this lane; no lease row is taken (no write scope); no store row is written by any run of this lane.
D5_noReactivateNoWriteNoDeploy.theCodePathStillHasToExist: item 5 asks for the refusal, which lives on the apply path, so the apply path is built and TESTED (violation, not observation) while never being executed against a store.

falsifiersPreRegistered.falsifier: 1. Pointed at Bastrop, the new sources' review reproduces P-212's live count within 1 percent.
falsifiersPreRegistered.preRegisteredAnswer: PASS expected, WITH A DENOMINATOR THAT MUST BE NAMED, because the two numbers are not the same population and letting them look like one would be the defect. P-212 released against a population of 57,704 retired rows and found 56,691 live. The store now holds 1,013 retired rows, because 56,691 of them were REACTIVATED by P-212 and are no longer retired. So the falsifier is decidable only as: the SAME live source, pointed at the SAME residual set, reproduces P-212's recorded verdict for that set. P-212 recorded 0 live / 1,013 absent for the residual (spot-checked). I predict confirmedLive = 0 and confirmedAbsent + unmeasured = 1,013, and I will report the residual's live SHARE (0/1013 = 0.00%) beside P-212's live share for the set it actually measured (56,691/57,704 = 98.24%) and state that the two are different bases. If the new sources find any of the 1,013 live, the falsifier FAILS in the most useful direction and P-212's residual is a false-retirement population after all.
falsifiersPreRegistered.howItWillBeEvidenced: the report-only run's own JSON for 48021, plus a replay of the same BCAD source over the 1,013 ids with the request count stated

falsifiersPreRegistered.falsifier: 2. A county whose live source is unreachable reports UNMEASURED, never zero candidates.
falsifiersPreRegistered.preRegisteredAnswer: PASS expected, proven by VIOLATION rather than observation: McLennan has NO registered source, so it exercises the none-registered branch; and the unit test drives a source that THROWS (transport failure) and a source that returns a non-JSON body, asserting every candidate lands in `unmeasured` with the reason, `confirmedAbsent` is empty, and the summary's `liveCurrencySource` reads 'unreachable'. The pre-change behaviour predicted in advance: on the branch point this same test would put every candidate in stillRetired with the reason 'NOT confirmed live', which is the false inference.
falsifiersPreRegistered.howItWillBeEvidenced: the new script test, plus the literal pre-change output captured by running the same fixture against origin/main's implementation (negative control)

falsifiersPreRegistered.falsifier: 3. The reactivation refusal fires on a synthetic run above the declared share (test).
falsifiersPreRegistered.preRegisteredAnswer: PASS expected, on the pure guard and on the CLI's own call site. Two parts: (a) `evaluateBlastRadius` refuses with BLAST_RADIUS_EXCEEDED when affected/priorRetired > 0.05 with no override, and passes with the exact token `BLAST_RADIUS_OVERRIDE=parcel-node-retired-review-reactivation:<fips>:<affected>/<population>`; (b) the CLI test asserts the refusal is raised BEFORE any write attempt, i.e. with affected above the threshold the run exits non-zero and the writer is never called. The pre-change behaviour predicted in advance: origin/main's CLI has no such call at all, so the negative control is that the same fixture writes.
